### 2026-10-12 – # Week 2 Starts!

**5h**

# Week 2 Starts!
I saw that this time there is a guide to create a "Merbl Run," and I was considering following it, but I decided not to since I want at least one of my submissions to be made without following the beginner guide. I think this week is the perfect opportunity to do this, since I think I will need the beginner guides for the other weeks... Instead, I am going to be building upon my Week 1 project, and creating the enclosure to the PCB! No school today because of Thanksgiving, so I was able to get a lot of work done ᕙ( •̀ ᗜ •́ )ᕗ
## What I did
- Before I actually got the 3D design part, I was doomscrolling on the Half Life page, and realized that somebody following the Starbie guide had components, such as the screen and the sensors, on their 3D renders. This surprised me, because I only had some of the components rendered, not all. I searched up how to get the rest of the renders, and I found out that I have to manually add them by finding a .step file for each. So that's what I did, and now I have the render with all of the components that will be in the final product. I did not know this at the time, but that was a crucial step to start making the enclosure, since I would have to know how tall everything is and where it physically goes, to make the depth or the holes of the enclosure the appropiate size. I also updated the [Week 1 Astrobie GitHub repository](https://github.com/avilldev/half-life-week1-PCB-Astrobie) to include that.

![Untitled drawing 6](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/5fce0ccc1df4d6e4eeab0c59dc913c592f6cd91459088abc9ea0c3564ef90b87.png)
- Now that I had the 3D renders, I realized that I had made a crucial mistake in the orientation of the ESP32 in the PCB Editor; it was facing sideways, towards the DHT11 sensor, meaning that if the components would be placed as it was, the USB-C cable would not fit in... I had to rotate the part, rewired the affected components, did the grounding again, and generated new Gerber files to fix this problem. I also updated the repository to include these updates.

![Untitled drawing 7](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/37bfd3a6dcc42da1274c569a28161235b0bc16c64d0f1ab5cbaa51cc8e960a95.png)
Now that the above problems were solved:
- Signed up to Onshape.
- Exported my PCB board with the 3D components as a .step file.
- Uploaded the .step file onto Onshape.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/432d374771761fbc8e158d6fa2172262af1b94dbdf589c5a7ab4b4ffb65662c2.png)
- Started creating the enclosure!
## The Enclosure
First I created the base of the enclosure. With the Use tool, I traced the UFO shape of the PCB. I also added a 0.5mm offset so that the PCB fits into the casing without major issues.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/ceba25920596cebe6875c5925e2f0fdab66e326616fa70ee44fb557c50b18171.png)
I created the solid 12mm deep base on the offset outline. This thickness ensures that the long pins have room below. The block was shelled so that it would have 2mm walls (growing outwards) and 2mm floor. I added some "pillars" in open spaces so that it can keep the PCB board suspended so the board sits completely flat and with room for the pins.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/adb1566447fc175bf39eac37c46ca5d391190382ccdde478d4000ac36f40e1e4.png)
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/ebce6eb9a0d933dc315ff1fe9c790c519e0352f11b291dd60f34136b079428df.png)
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/ba5e26c3a7b7aaed6ba3459ae00ec601c3ef2a0bb24117c21b7b9c3967e0c87e.png)

I also started creating a 2mm lid, separate from the base. On this lid, I traced rectangular areas for the pieces that are sticking out, such as the pushbuttons, the DHT11 sensor, the pins for the MPU6050, and on top of the screen so it can actually be seen.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/1ef67e7511102f2a3d884ee14d388addefb2c02d87f3cbcc805d8d1dac6564c7.png)

## What I have to do next
- Do the 5 hours progress reel
- I have to cut a hole so that the USB-C cable can be connected to the ESP32.
- Add round, smooth corners
- Prepare the printing files!

### 2026-10-14 – # Progressing!

**3h**

# Progressing!
## What I did
- Previously I made the holes for the top of the lid, so that you could see the screen, and some components, such as the DHT11or the push buttons, could go through. Today, I created a hole on the side so that the cable can go through and connect to the USB-C port attached to the ESP32.

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 185144](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/93423e3bc3bb280feca323adcf920dbf8674e7b8566a739aa937ad3424460cab.png)
- I also started thinking about more of the aesthetics of the enclosure, so I rounded off some of the edges using the Fillet tool. I rounded the edges on the side, top of the lid, bottom of the base, and the hole for the screen. It looks waay better than I thought it would :D

![Screenshot 2026-10-14 185847](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/a283198065c47221cabd5a276536620456f2a0941dc9ec824e0dcf9e5ce975fa.png)
- I thought about rounding the edges of the hole for the USB-C, but it would look uneven, since I could not fillet the top part since it was already filleted... unfortunate, but maybe I come up with something else.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/d75e01aab475009995620e47996d5f53218d2a0621d7fdac031fdc9ee304a1bf.png)
- Apart from that, I thought that everything was pretty much set, but then I realized that the the lid will not be able to sit on top correctly, since some of the components within the MPU6050 were sticking out over the top of the base...

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/d1309ca7e951428e593025e643cf934ac0bf6a3e35b24a3363454ae1c7e88536.png)
The solution to me seemed like I would have to just make the base taller. Then I realized that if I do that, not only would that problem be solved, but perhaps I would be able to round the edges for the USB-C window!

I was able to fix that problem relatively easily, by making the extrusion that puts up the wall higher. From the sideview, it can be seen that anything that does not have a designated hole to go through will be properly covered up by the lid.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/e1cb440aa2082bba36798e6009e8523edd1e92b753fe5e85c7c5b27c580a3e23.png)
Indeed, now this also means that I can make the edges for the USB-C window curved!! So I got that done.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/6ea9fa011adb664cc4a2d9a4a5ebe63db9221345d33c3e6b800609b8eb1d1b92.png)
I also thought that it would be appropriate to round the edges for the holes for the buttons. And also for the other holes to keep it consistent :p. So now, my features (on the left side) are full of fillets 🐟🐟

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/0c9f0c86ab47dcb3db45520400942072d3a29962fbf820d5178c74edf2ae2d2e.png)
- Today, I was wondering what I would have to put on the BOM for this week, since it isn't really pre-made components that I am buying. I asked on the Hackclub Slack, in the #half-life channel, and I was told that I would have to find a 3D Printing Service provider. That makes so much sense xd! So I found one that is based near me, and got an idea on how much it would cost, and honestly, it's not that bad! My project is not done yet, but I think that it is a good idea to have an idea on how much the project is costing as I progress through the design process.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/s5X6uAidfBv2Me3zVHdgxREVUKqtvsIM/ff9186efb172346614f72350cf920480fb514cc235c739370cac336e717d2231.png)
## What to do next session.
That's all from today. Next session, I will:
- Look into a way to actually attach the lid to the base. Maybe screws, maybe something similar to LEGO, I'll see.
- Decorating the lid with drawings, since I am realizing now that with the lid, all the designs on the PCB (the silkscreen) will not be visible...
